d:T673,
<h2 class="text-2xl font-bold text-foreground mt-12 mb-4">What Is an SSN?</h2>

<p class="text-muted-foreground leading-relaxed mb-4">A Social Security Number (SSN) is issued to US citizens, permanent residents, and authorized temporary residents. It is used for employment, taxes, and Social Security benefits.</p>

<h2 class="text-2xl font-bold text-foreground mt-12 mb-4">What Is an ITIN?</h2>

<p class="text-muted-foreground leading-relaxed mb-4">An Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) is issued to non-residents and others who need a US tax ID but cannot get an SSN.</p>

<h2 class="text-2xl font-bold text-foreground mt-12 mb-4">Key Differences</h2>

<h3 class="text-xl font-semibold text-foreground mt-8 mb-3">Employment</h3>
<li class="ml-6 text-muted-foreground">SSN: Required for legal employment in the US</li>
<li class="ml-6 text-muted-foreground">ITIN: Cannot be used for employment</li>

<h3 class="text-xl font-semibold text-foreground mt-8 mb-3">Tax Filing</h3>
<li class="ml-6 text-muted-foreground">SSN: Used to file taxes and claim credits</li>
<li class="ml-6 text-muted-foreground">ITIN: Used to file taxes only</li>

<h3 class="text-xl font-semibold text-foreground mt-8 mb-3">Benefits</h3>
<li class="ml-6 text-muted-foreground">SSN: Qualifies for Social Security benefits</li>
<li class="ml-6 text-muted-foreground">ITIN: No Social Security benefits</li>

<h3 class="text-xl font-semibold text-foreground mt-8 mb-3">Eligibility</h3>
<li class="ml-6 text-muted-foreground">SSN: US citizens and authorized residents only</li>
<li class="ml-6 text-muted-foreground">ITIN: Available to non-residents worldwide</li>
